title: Speed vs. Velocity
subcategory: Mechanics — Motion in a Straight Line

references.label: NCERT Physics Part I, Class 11 — Motion in a Straight Line

summary: Speed is the rate of change of distance with time (a scalar). Velocity is the rate of change of displacement with time (a vector).
explanation: Because speed is built from distance and velocity is built from displacement, the same distinction carries over: speed is always positive (or zero) and never accounts for direction, while velocity carries a direction and can be positive, negative, or zero depending on the choice of reference direction. Average speed over a trip can differ from the magnitude of average velocity whenever the path isn't a straight line in one direction — average speed uses total distance divided by total time, while average velocity uses net displacement divided by total time.

comparison.right: Yes, depending on chosen positive direction

commonMisconceptions: Treating 'average speed' and 'average velocity' as interchangeable numbers for round trips or curved paths.
examples: A car completing a round trip has a nonzero average speed but zero average velocity (net displacement is zero).
genZNote: Speed tells you how fast. Velocity tells you how fast and which way — physics really said direction matters.
